result.topic_en: Evaluation of log(2K/π) at the special points x = (m/n)π (n odd, m odd) and x = (m/2n)π (m odd), with α = e^{2πi/4n}, reducing double sums to finite sums of the sawtooth function ((·)) with mμ ≡ 1.

$\log\frac{2K}{\pi}=\frac{q+q_0}{q-q_0}\frac{\pi^2}{4n^2}+\log\frac{q_0+q}{q_0-q}+2\sum\sum_{1,4n-1}^{s}\frac{1}{4nt+s}\cdot\frac{\alpha^{2ms}-1}{\alpha^{2ms}+1}$
$=A+2\int_0^1\sum_{1,4n}^{t}\frac{\alpha^t dx}{1-\alpha^t x}\cdot\frac{1}{4n}\cdot-\frac{1}{2n}\sum_{1,4n-1}^{s}\sum_{0,2n-1}^{\sigma}(-1)^\sigma\sigma\alpha^{2s\sigma m}(\alpha^{2ms}+1)\alpha^{-ts}$
[-1) $t\equiv 2ms \mod. 4n$-]

$=A+2\int_0^1\sum_{1,4n}^{t}\frac{\alpha^t dx}{1-\alpha^t x}\cdot\frac{1}{4n}\cdot 2\sum_{1,4n-1}^{s}\sum_{1,2n-1}^{\sigma}(-1)^\sigma\left(\frac{\sigma-n}{2n}\right)\alpha^{2ms\sigma}\alpha^{-ts}$
1) $t\equiv 2mr \mod. 4n$
2) $t\equiv 2mr+2n$
$=A-2\sum_{1,2n-1}\log(1-\alpha^{2mr})\frac{1}{4n}\cdot(-1)^r\left(\frac{r-n}{2n}\right)4n+2\sum\log(1-\alpha^{2mr+2n})(-1)^r\left(\frac{r-n}{2n}\right)$
$=A-2\pi i\sum_{1,2n-1}(-1)^r\left(\left(\frac{mr+n}{2n}\right)-\left(\frac{mr}{2n}\right)\right)\left(\frac{r-n}{2n}\right)$
$=A-2\pi i\sum_{1,2n-1}(-1)^r\left(\left(\frac{r+n}{2n}\right)-\left(\frac{r}{2n}\right)\right)\left(\frac{\mu r-n}{2n}\right)$, $m\mu\equiv 1 \mod. 2n$
$=A+2\pi i\sum_{1,n-1}(-1)^r\left(\frac{\mu r-n}{2n}\right)$
3) $x=\frac{m}{2n}\pi$, $m$ ungerade.
$\log\frac{2K}{\pi}=\log\frac{q_0+q}{q_0-q}+2\sum\sum_{1,4n-1}^{s}\frac{1}{4nt+s}\cdot\frac{\alpha^{ms}-1}{\alpha^{ms}+1}$
$=A+2\int_0^1\sum_{1,2n}^{t}\frac{\alpha^t dx}{1-\alpha^t x}\cdot\frac{1}{4n}\cdot 2\sum_{1,4n-1}^{s}\sum_{1,4n-1}^{\sigma}(-1)^\sigma\left(\frac{\sigma-2n}{4n}\right)\alpha^{ms\sigma}\alpha^{-ts}$
$=A+2\pi i\sum_{1,2n-1}(-1)^r\left(\frac{\mu r-2n}{4n}\right)$, $m\mu\equiv 1 \mod. 4n$

methods.what: Expansion of log(2K/π) near x = (m/n)π as a double series with terms (α^{2ms}-1)/(α^{2ms}+1), α a 4n-th root of unity
Representing 1/(4nt+s) sums via an integral of geometric series and finite Fourier expansion of (α^{2ms}-1)/(α^{2ms}+1) in terms of the sawtooth function
Splitting by residue classes of t and summing to logarithms of 1-α^k
Reduction to Dedekind-sum-like finite sum of sawtooth values, using inverse μ of m
Final result for case 2 (n odd, m odd)
Expansion for case 3, x=(m/2n)π, m odd
Final result for case 3 as finite sawtooth sum with mμ≡1 mod 4n
